text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Joseph Kamotho, secretary-general of the ruling Kenya African National Union party, denies the government is harassing members of the Masai community.
- The government increases the capital base of the civil contingency fund to two billion shillings from 30 million shillings in the face of possible famine.
- A policeman is charged with the murder of a Roman Catholic monk shot dead on Tuesday at a school in Njoro town near Nakuru.
- The chairman of the standing committee on Human Rights in Kenya says senior government officials and some political leaders are the major culprits in abusing the rights of Kenyans.
- Mombasa customs officials seal off 18 warehouses suspected of containing goods worth billions of shillings on which customs duties were not paid.
- The government halts investment in the sugar industry in Kenya to give local and international investors opportunities to set up businesses.
- A cargo ship loaded with 7,300 metric tonnes of Brazilian white crystal sugar worth 365 million shillings is denied entry to the port of Mombasa because of a lack of documentation.
- Opposition leader Raila Odinga's lawyer applies to change his civil suit seeking a declaration that the chief justice has reached retirement age. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
